# The NewCO: What, Why, and How?

*New Conscientious Objector (NewCO), 2026-01-03* · [Original post](https://newconscientiousobjector.com/2026/01/03/the-newco-what-why-and-how/)[^original-post]

### **WHAT Is Offered**

The **NewCO (New Conscientious Objector)** framework provides a comprehensive strategic blueprint for the immediate **cessation of systemic sin** within the Iowa Yearly Meeting (Conservative) tradition. The NewCO is about a **faithful response** composed of three integrated pillars: **LANDBACK, Mutual Aid, and Abolition.**

The NewCO offers the institutional structure for **Communal Risk Absorption** through a working group on **Decolonial Repair,** which is modeled after the historical Meetings for Sufferings. Furthermore, the NewCO suggests developing LANDBACK research protocols to investigate property title histories and identify original Indigenous stewardship. Truth-telling workshops and new Queries for discernment are suggested to acknowledge historical complicity.

### **WHY It Is Important**

This framework is essential because it addresses the fused architecture of Christian Colonial Capitalist Violence (CCV), which reinforces a **self-perpetuating loop** of **ideological license, land theft, and economic extraction.** It solves the crisis of the “economic draft,” a system that conscripts labor, money, and daily life into structures of environmental and racial destruction. By adopting the NewCO model, we ensure that modern efforts do not repeat the cultural genocide of Quaker-run Indian Boarding Schools. Implementing these actions actively **disrupts “Settler Futurity”** by **refusing the assumption that the colonial state and its extraction-based economy are permanent or inevitable.**

### **HOW It Is Measured**

**Success is quantified through specific material benchmarks** rather than symbolic statements or performative acknowledgments. Measured results include the **dollar amount of wealth transferred** directly to Indigenous control via Voluntary Land Taxes and the Honor Native Land Fund. Progress is tracked by **the number of community members whose daily survival needs are met** through autonomous **Mutual Aid** pods outside of capitalist market logic. Effectiveness in Abolition is measured by the **reduction in police reliance** for conflict resolution and the number of individuals freed from cages through community bail funds. **Institutional integrity** is confirmed by the completion of **LANDBACK** research on acreage, such as the land occupied by Scattergood Friends School, and the subsequent transfer of title or jurisdiction to Indigenous nations. Finally, success is seen in the adoption of a new Query on Complicity and Repair into the official *Advices and Queries*.

#### **Quaker Insights**

* **Embrace Immediatism:** Delaying justice through committees is an act of spiritual disobedience; once a sin like the occupation of stolen land is identified, it must be stopped immediately.
* **Utilize the Surgeon Analogy:** Just as a surgeon must immediately cut out a lethal infection to save a life, the Meeting must decisively rupture its ties with CCV to preserve its spiritual health.
* **Establish a Faithful Remnant:** If the larger corporate body chooses the path of Gradualism, individuals must follow the 1877 Bear Creek precedent by acting as a “faithful remnant” to preserve the integrity of the witness.
* **Prioritize Institutional Self-Abnegation:** True integrity requires ceding institutional resources and power directly to Indigenous-led efforts, acknowledging that the needs of the harmed community are more important than the institution’s own functions.
* **Adopt the Symmetrical Antidote:** Because systemic violence is fused, the response must be equally integrated; one cannot faithfully pursue peace without also pursuing LANDBACK and Mutual Aid.
* **Withdraw from the Economic Draft:** Consistency of faith requires a total refusal of the socio-economic systems of violence, recognizing that daily participation in extractive capitalism is a form of spiritual collaboration with war.

# Targets of the Economic Draft

*New Conscientious Objector (NewCO), 2026-01-07* · [Original post](https://newconscientiousobjector.com/2026/01/07/targets-of-the-economic-draft/)[^original-post]

### Conscription by Survival

New understanding of how the draft for military service has evolved since the Vietnam war has surprised me. I knew the All Voluntary Army was meant to replace the draft. I knew many people have served multiple tours of duty.

The **Economic Draft** is the primary method of **Christian Colonial Capitalist Violence (CCV)**, functioning as a system of **“conscription by survival”** that replaces the legislative statutes of the past with the “mute compulsion of economic relations”. This system weaponizes basic human needs—**food, shelter, and medicine**—to compel labor for extractive and militaristic industries. It operates through **a strategy of coercion that leaves the individual with an intentional absence of alternatives.**

#### Targeted Groups of the Economic Draft

**1. The Disenfranchised: The Poverty Draft** This mechanism captures those with the fewest options for training or employment, creating a “poverty pipeline” into the military-industrial complex. Recruitment efforts are not evenly distributed; they are aggressively concentrated in communities with low median incomes where the promise of a steady paycheck, healthcare, and education is an offer many cannot refuse. In low-income areas of cities like Detroit and Los Angeles, JROTC enrollment rates reach between 75 and 100 percent of the student body, functioning as a direct channel from impoverished backgrounds into the armed forces. **The state leverages the high cost of education and the scarcity of living-wage jobs to ensure a constant supply of labor for its global hegemony.**

**2. The Working Class: Job Lock** The working and middle classes are captured through the anomaly of tying healthcare to employment. **“Job lock” is the inability of an employee to leave an undesirable position due to the fear of losing health insurance or retirement benefits.** This restriction of labor mobility prevents individuals from pursuing “NewCO” vocations—such as community organizing or sustainable farming—that do not offer corporate benefits. Statistical analysis reveals that up to 64.6% of workers experience job lock due to insurance concerns, while approximately 75% report job lock due to monetary constraints. **This coercion forces daily compromises of conscience, as people labor in industries that degrade the environment simply to secure medical care for their families.**

**3. The Educated Class: Indentured Servitude** Debt, specifically student loan debt, functions as a modern form of indentured servitude for the educated class. As investment in public education collapses, students must take on massive debts to acquire necessary credentials. **This debt acts as a disciplining force; graduates with significant debt are less likely to choose low-paying vocations in social justice and are instead compelled to seek employment in high-paying corporate or defense sectors to service their loans.** With student debt now exceeding $1.7 trillion, the state effectively conscripts the nation’s intellectual capital to maintain the financial status quo and the war economy.

# Economic draft and NewCO

*New Conscientious Objector (NewCO), 2026-01-08* · [Original post](https://newconscientiousobjector.com/2026/01/08/economic-draft-and-newco/)[^original-post]

The **economic draft** is the **enforcement** mechanism of the broader system of colonial capitalism. Unlike the legislative conscription of the 20th century, which used legal mandates and the threat of prison, this contemporary draft leverages economic conditions to force participation in extractive and militaristic industries. The **New Conscientious Objector (NewCO)** is the response to this entrapment, that refuses participation in the entire fused architecture of systemic violence.

#### The Overarching System: Colonial Capitalism

![](https://i0.wp.com/newconscientiousobjector.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/01/image-6.png)

* **Mutual Aid** provides the necessary “rations”—unconditional food and care—that allow a person to “desert” the economic draft without facing starvation.
* **Abolition** removes the carceral enforcers who protect the property relations of the draft through evictions and the criminalization of poverty.
* Finally, **LANDBACK** provides the foundation for a **Social Solidarity Economy (SSE)** that functions outside the logic of the market, addressing the original theft that enabled market dependency.

# A wider view

*New Conscientious Objector (NewCO), 2026-01-10* · [Original post](https://newconscientiousobjector.com/2026/01/10/a-wider-view/)[^original-post]

Yesterday, when I wrote **[Who is colonized now?](https://newconscientiousobjector.com/2026/01/09/who-is-colonized-now/)** I was in no way suggesting a false equivalency with those who have suffered from colonialism from the first day the Europeans came to these lands centuries ago.

My focus for months now has been on the consequences of the colonization of this land. For many reasons.

But now, the rapid collapse of the current political and economic systems, with increasing authoritarianism has devolved into **state violence** against us all, the general public.

**Those of us who were among the privileged of this country, find that we no longer are.** And because we hadn’t had to adapt to oppressive conditions, we are bewildered about how to respond to this violence directed at us.

Adopting the concepts of the **NewCO (new conscientious objector)** is how we can respond.

#### Economic Draft

The concept of the “Economic draft” is helpful here because it shows how huge groups of people are forced to stay in jobs that they aren’t invested in or don’t believe in. Young people from economically disadvantaged communities are targeted by military recruiters. Millions of people are tied to such jobs because they need the healthcare insurance. And millions of others are trapped in jobs they don’t want because they have huge student debt.

![](https://i0.wp.com/newconscientiousobjector.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/01/image.png)

---

#### The NewCO

Those who have historically been oppressed have been building alternative solutions. The concept of the **NewCO (new conscientious objector)** provides an integrate way to look at these systems, and the solutions to address them.

![](https://i0.wp.com/newconscientiousobjector.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/01/image-10.png)

---

This integrated concept is profoundly counter-intuitive because it challenges us to stop seeing these issues as separate struggles—such as racism, economic inequality, and militarism—and instead see them as one integrated system that must be confronted as a whole.

#### **The Ultimate Strategy: Make the System Obsolete by Building a Better One**

And the best thing about this solution (NewCO) is that it doesn’t waste time and effort trying to make incremental changes in systems that are themselves the sources of injustice. **You cannot create justice as long as you are embedded in the systems of injustice.**

The integrated solution of **LANDBACK, Mutual Aid, and Abolition** of police and prisons is what I have been led to believe is the only just response.

With **LANDBACK** as the foundation, the NewCO strategy uses Mutual Aid and Abolition to build a functioning alternative that makes the Economic Draft irrelevant.

**Mutual Aid** is the logistical engine of this new world, operating under the principle of “Solidarity, Not Charity.” Unlike charity, which is vertical, mutual aid is a horizontal, reciprocal practice of people working together to meet collective needs. The Des Moines Mutual Aid (DMMA) “Panther Pantry,” a weekly free food giveaway that I was involved in, is a concrete example of “People’s Infrastructure.” It provides the material “rations”—unconditional food, housing, and care—that allow individuals to “desert” the war economy. These rations directly counter the coercion of the **Poverty Draft** by meeting basic needs and nullify **Job Lock** by creating community safety nets independent of employers.

**Abolition** is the strategy of “Systemic Non-Collaboration”—a total refusal to grant legitimacy to the police and prisons, which are the “domestic enforcement arm of the war machine.” This is not a passive stance but a dual strategy of systematically divesting from systems of harm while simultaneously investing in community-based systems of genuine safety and transformative justice. By refusing their legitimacy, Abolition dismantles the state’s power to execute the evictions and criminalize the poverty that the Economic Draft weaponizes.

This is why I’ve been led to the concept of the **NewCO (new conscientious objector)**, because that is the response to CCV. It isn’t important that people use the term NewCO, but I’ve been led to that term because it reflects a conscientious objection approach for today, based upon the concept of conscientious objection to war in the past. The NewCO is about **mutual aid, LANDBACK and the Abolition of police and prisons.** Thus far, I’ve been writing mostly about mutual aid, and about LANDBACK.

![](https://i0.wp.com/newconscientiousobjector.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/01/Ronnie-James-1.png)

#### Abolition

Most people are apprehensive when they hear about the abolition of police and prisons. They think they are safer with policing and prisons. Most see prisons as a way to remove ‘criminals’ from society.

But the current escalation of policing violence is showing the fallacy of relying on police for safety to those who didn’t already know.

Those of us who are old enough remember that when we were growing up that there was very little police presence in our communities. There were no mega-prisons or the routine use of solitary confinement. No prisons for profit. No school to prison pipeline.

The New Conscientious Objector (NewCO) recognizes that the modern **Peace Testimony** must expand beyond a refusal of military service to a withdrawal of consent from the entire carceral state. Because the carceral state is a form of systemic, state-sanctioned warfare against the poor and marginalized, a NewCO responds by divesting from these violent institutions and investing in community-based alternatives like the Great Plains Action Society’s Healing Justice House, or Bear Creek meeting’s work on a mental health center.

> Abolition is the removal of the enforcer. Without the police to enforce the threat of destitution, the state loses its power of coercion. Mutual Aid provides the “rations” that allow a NewCO to desert the **Economic Draft**, while Abolition removes the enforcers who would punish that desertion. (see more about the **Economic Draft** here: **<https://newconscientiousobjector.com/?s=economic+draft> )**

#### The abolition of police and prisons is an expansion of the Quaker Peace Testimony.

![](https://i0.wp.com/newconscientiousobjector.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/01/image-12.png)

Integrity demands that we recognize the “Pennsylvania System” as a catastrophic failure of benevolent intent. We must now work to dismantle the very carceral structures our ancestors helped build.

Quaker’s belief in “that of God in everyone” is fundamentally incompatible with a system that cages human beings for being poor. The NewCO understands that freedom is not merely emancipation from a cell, but the creation of a Social Solidarity Economy that **makes the state’s monopoly on care irrelevant**. When we build a Community Land Trust or a “Panther Pantry,” we are engaged in the spiritual work of taking away the occasion of war by removing the economic weapons used against our neighbors. Our Meetinghouses could become hubs for this response, to become active sites of sanctuary and supply.

Modern American prisons originated from Quaker ideology, specifically William Penn’s “Great Law” of 1682, which established rehabilitation over punishment as the primary goal. However, this legacy proves that the same Quaker principles that sought humane reform ultimately contributed to creating the modern penitentiary system that many contemporary Quakers now view as fundamentally flawed. Canadian Quakers made history in 1981 by becoming the first religious body to call for complete prison abolition, declaring that **“the imprisonment of human beings, like their enslavement, is inherently immoral”.** This position represents a radical evolution from our ancestors’ support for prison reform to complete rejection of incarceration as a solution.

# National Quaker Conference on the Draft 1968

*New Conscientious Objector (NewCO), 2026-02-07* · [Original post](https://newconscientiousobjector.com/2026/02/07/national-quaker-conference-on-the-draft-1968/)[^original-post]

The situation in Minneapolis provides clear examples of the violence of rapidly evolving state **authoritarianism**. And has shown surprising and effective responses to the violence by the people there. Demonstrating the concepts of the **NewCO** (new conscientious objector) and ‘**active objection**.’

#### Significance of Minneapolis

I’m bringing this up in the context of the violence of militarized policing in Minneapolis. Because of the amazing, peaceful and effective responses from the people there. Demonstrating a shift from **resistance** to ‘**active objection**‘, instead.

![](https://i0.wp.com/newconscientiousobjector.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/02/unnamed-2026-02-01T080536.881.png)

---

#### The 1968 Richmond Declaration redefined non-compliance

I’m telling the story about the 1968 Richmond Declaration on the Draft and Conscription here, because that represented a significant change is how (some) Quakers thought about our **responses to war**. The result was a call to reject the privileges Quakers often received, allowing them to do two years of alternative civilian service instead of combat. And **calls for the abolition of conscription itself**.

In high school (class of 1970) I spent a lot of time studying and praying about what I should do about the requirement for males to register with the Selective Service System, the military draft, when we turn 18 years-of-age. I was aware of the significance of this decision, which would, and did, determine which path my life would follow.

I saw the draft decision as a **choice** between doing what I believed was right or taking the easy way out. Was I willing to risk imprisonment by turning in my draft card, or would I consent to do two years of alternative (civilian) service under the Selective Service System?

I knew Quaker men who were **imprisoned** for **refusing** to **cooperate** with the miliary. One was a classmate of mine from Scattergood Friends School. I turned in my draft card, but wasn’t prosecuted for doing so. Our stories, and those of other Quakers facing conscription were collected by Iowa Quaker, **Don Laughlin** (see below).

A national conference of Quakers met at Earlham College in Richmond, Indiana, in 1968, to consider what Quakers should do in the face of the Vietnam War. I attended that conference, representing Scattergood Friends School.

#### An historic shift in Quaker thought and practice

The 1968 Richmond Declaration redefined non-compliance by rejecting the “privileged status” of traditional Conscientious Objection and calling for the **total abolition** of the conscription system itself.

**Friends Coordinating Committee on Peace has announced a national conference on the draft and conscription to be held at Earlham College (Richmond, Indiana), October 11th through 13th. It is primarily planned as a working conference, with about 180 representatives from Yearly Meetings, Friends schools and other Friends’ organizations and seventy to a hundred additional Friends appointed at large. A detailed program and other information may be obtained from FCCP, 1520 Race Street, Philadelphia, 19102.**
***Friends Journal 8/15/1968***

---

We call on Friends everywhere to recognize the oppressive burden of militarism and conscription. We acknowledge our complicity in these evils in ways sometimes silent and subtle, at times painfully apparent. We are under obligation as Children of God and members of the Religious Society of Friends to break the yoke of that complicity.

**As Friends we have for many years been granted privileged status within the draft system. This has often blinded us to the evil of the draft itself, and the treatment of those not so privileged. We are grateful for all those who by resolutely resisting the draft have quickened our conscience. We are called into the community of all who suffer for their refusal to perform unconscionable acts.**

***Declaration on the Draft and Conscription, Richmond 1968***

### **From Privilege to Abolition**

**The 1968 Richmond Declaration redefined non-compliance by rejecting the “privileged status” of traditional Conscientious Objection and calling for the total abolition of the conscription system itself.**

**1. The Rejection of Privilege** The Declaration acknowledged that the special status granted to Quakers (Conscientious Objector classification) had “blinded” the community to the evil of the draft itself. It redefined non-compliance not as seeking a personal exemption from sin, but as refusing to accept a privilege that was denied to the poor and non-religious. The signatories believed that cooperating with the draft, even as a recognized CO, made one “part of the power which forces our brothers into the military”.

**2. From Reform to Abolition** The Declaration explicitly stated, “We do not support efforts at draft reform; the issue is not equal treatment under compulsion, but freedom from compulsion”. This shifted the goal from making the draft “fairer” for pacifists to making the draft obsolete. It committed the body to work for the total “abolition of the Selective Service System” rather than seeking comfortable niches within it.

**3. Active Non-Cooperation** The Declaration moved beyond “Static Objection” (refusal to carry a gun) to “Active Objection” (refusal to cooperate with the logistics of conscription). It urged Friends to refuse to register, to return draft cards, and to refuse to fill out Selective Service forms. This validated the view that “fidelity to Truth” required breaking the law when the law itself was a mechanism of oppression.

**4. Institutional Support (Meeting for Sufferings)** It redefined the role of the Meeting from a place of passive worship to a hub of risk absorption. The Declaration called for the establishment of “Meetings for Sufferings” to provide bail, legal aid, jobs, and shelter for those who faced prison for their non-cooperation. This effectively operationalized the concept of “Communal Risk Absorption,” ensuring that individuals did not face the Enforcer alone.

*New Conscientious Objector (NewCO), 2026-02-10* · [Original post](https://newconscientiousobjector.com/2026/02/10/signs-and-witness/)[^original-post]

The American Friends Service Committee (AFSC) is calling for Quakers and other people of faith to participate in ongoing monthly public, silent demonstrations [**to share witness against rising authoritarianism and oppression in the United States.**](https://afsc.org/love-action)

![](https://i0.wp.com/newconscientiousobjector.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/02/image-7.png)

This is one of the signs AFSC provides for this witness. It immediately brought back memories of my experiences with numerous vigils I’ve been part of in. This began for me when I was a student at Scattergood Friends School in 1969, when Iowa Quaker Don Laughlin invited me to join a weekly vigil in downtown Iowa City.

#### Signs for Another Witness

When Michael Brown was killed in 2014, I was part of a group that was called **Indy10**, referring to the ten people from Indianapolis who went to Ferguson right after Michael Brown’s death, taking water and supplies and a willingness to help. There was intense unrest after Michael’s shooting. It was the first time we saw military equipment deployed on our streets. The group was fiercely committed to act for social change.

This is a photo of one member of Indy10, JR, that I took during one of our many public demonstrations:

![](https://i0.wp.com/newconscientiousobjector.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/02/stopkillingblackpeople.jpg)

#### Black Lives Have Always Mattered

This is from blog posts I wrote at the time, **[Black Lives Have Always Mattered.](https://quakersandreligioussocialism.com/2022/02/01/black-lives-have-always-mattered/)**

Racial justice, and Black Lives Matter, need vocal, visible and spiritual support from White Quakers now. How often has the Underground Railroad been invoked during discussions of Friends and enslavement and racial justice? Have you wondered what you would have done if you had been alive then? Twenty years from now what will you remember when you think back to this time and what you did, or did not do?

When I was living in Indianapolis, I attended the peace vigil every Friday afternoon in downtown Indianapolis. There were usually just three or four attending. We held signs about peace, including the Friends Committee on National Legislation’s ‘War is Not the Answer’.

I had been thinking a lot about peace building and felt that addressing economic, environmental and racial injustice is what constitutes peace building today in the United States.

After Michael Brown’s killing in 2014, and the ongoing killings of people of color, there were multiple demonstrations in Indianapolis.

I changed my message to **Quakers Black Lives Matter.** I made the sign below to take to our weekly peace vigil in front of the Federal Building in downtown Indianapolis. I was very unsure of how that sign would be received by people of any race, but felt called to do it

However, I had forgotten the first time I carried the sign to the vigil (I didn’t own a car) was the weekend of Indy Black Expo. As I was walking to the Federal Building and entered the downtown mall, I was suddenly in the middle of thousands of people of color. I was unsure of what the reaction would be. I was tempted to turn around and go home. But I mostly got looks of surprise and puzzlement. No one said anything then (there was music, food, etc.).

But during the hour of the peace vigil that day, there were a lot of interactions, both with people driving and those walking past our group of three, and they were all positive. Many people said “thanks” with smiles. Someone said, “that’s a good sign, a damn good sign”. “Our lives DO matter”, said another.

![](https://kislingjeff.files.wordpress.com/2021/03/dd6c8-jeff_blm1.jpg)

Carrying the sign on the way home after the peace vigil, I was surprised by the sound of an air horn, and looked up into the cab of the tractor trailer passing by, where two young black men were grinning and waving their arms.

**Another day a young Black man stopped, got out of his car, and walked up to us. I wasn’t sure how that was going to go. But he said, “a white man holding a Black Lives Matter sign”. I said, “yes, a white man holding a Black Lives Matter Sign”. He started to go away, but returned and asked, “why are you doing it?” I told him about the Kheprw Institute (KI) that mentors Black youth that I had been involved with for several years now. And how those kids had become friends of mine. And I want a better life for them. He nodded, then said it was a brave thing to do. I only mention this to show how other people might see what you do in public. He went on to say he felt justice had to be grounded in faith.**

Many times a car of people of color would honk, and people smile and cheer and wave their hands. Many times taking photos with their phones.

Another day an energetic young Black man came and said “Quakers, Black Lives Matter”, and began to take a video of us, then had a friend take more video as he stood with his arms around our shoulders, narrating all the time–“Quakers”, “Black Lives Matter”.

Bear Creek Friend Jenny Cisar created this decal and made 100 copies, which people were eager to obtain.

*New Conscientious Objector (NewCO), 2026-02-11* · [Original post](https://newconscientiousobjector.com/2026/02/11/a-dozen-roses-for-renee-good/)[^original-post]

Jan 12, 2026. This story of spontaneous connections between all kinds of people begins at the site of Renee’s death and is still expanding, carrying us together into our future. It is a healing balm, a gift of restoration and resiliency, as we move forward to disassemble the replication of Nazism that is gripping the US government. Written and Narrated by Elder Kaia Svien

#### **Spirit Walking in the Tundra**

All the way to Nome, I trace the shadow of the plane as it walks Over turquoise lakes made by late spring breakup Of the Bering Sea. The plane is so heavy with cargo load it vibrates our bones. Like the pressure made by light cracking ice.

Below I see pockets of marrow where seabirds nest. Mothers are so protective they will dive humans. I walk from the tarmac and am met by an old friend. We drive to the launching place And see walrus hunters set out toward the sea. We swing to the summer camps where seal hangs on drying frames. She takes me home. I watch her son play video games on break from the university.

**This is what it feels like, says her son, as we walk up tundra, Toward a herd of musk ox, when you spirit walk. There is a shaking, and then you are in mystery.**

Little purple flowers come up from the permafrost. A newborn musk ox staggers around its mother’s legs.

I smell the approach of someone with clean thoughts. She is wearing designs like flowers, and a fur of ice. She carries a basket and digging implements. Her smell is sweet like blossoms coming up through the snow. **The spirit of the tundra stands with us, and we collect sunlight together, We are refreshed by small winds.**

We do not need history in books to tell us who we are Or where we come from, I remind him. **Up here, we are near the opening in the Earth’s head, the place where the spirit leaves and returns.** Up here, the edge between life and death is thinner than dried animal bladder.

(FOR ANUQSRAAQ AND QITUVITUAQ) NOME, ALASKA, 2011*Harjo, Joy. Conflict Resolution for Holy Beings: Poems (pp. 34-35). W. W. Norton & Company. Kindle Edition.*

***For Calling the Spirit Back from Wandering the Earth in Its Human Feet*** (excerpts)

Do not hold regrets.
When you find your way to the circle, to the fire kept burning by the keepers of your soul, you will be welcomed.
You must clean yourself with cedar, sage, or other healing plant.
Cut the ties you have to failure and shame.
Let go the pain you are holding in your mind, your shoulders, your heart, all the way to your feet. Let go the pain of your ancestors to make way for those who are heading in our direction.
Ask for forgiveness.
Call upon the help of those who love you. These helpers take many forms: animal, element, bird, angel, saint, stone, or ancestor.
Call your spirit back. It may be caught in corners and creases of shame, judgment, and human abuse.
You must call in a way that your spirit will want to return. Speak to it as you would to a beloved child.
Welcome your spirit back from its wandering. It may return in pieces, in tatters. Gather them together. They will be happy to be found after being lost for so long.
Then, you must do this: help the next person find their way through the dark.

**Harjo, Joy. Conflict Resolution for Holy Beings: Poems (pp. 5-6). W. W. Norton & Company. Kindle Edition.**

# Signs and Witness 2

*New Conscientious Objector (NewCO), 2026-02-12* · [Original post](https://newconscientiousobjector.com/2026/02/12/signs-and-witness-2/)[^original-post]

The American Friends Service Committee (AFSC) is calling for Quaker **[public witness to bring attention to the cruel and authoritarian actions in this country.](https://afsc.org/newsroom/love-action-bearing-witness-choosing-resistance-building-hope)**

This has led me to reflect on some of my experiences with public witness in the past. Thinking specifically about public interactions related to signs. **[I recently wrote about my experiences](https://newconscientiousobjector.com/2026/02/10/signs-and-witness/)** related to the sign I held during weekly peace vigils in Indianapolis. The sign read, **“Quakers Know Black Lives Matter.”**

![](https://i0.wp.com/newconscientiousobjector.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/02/Quakers-know-Black-Lives-Matter.png)

---

#### Defund DAPL

I’m now thinking about another experience I had when I held a sign that read, **“CHASE and PNC fund Dakota Pipeline.”** This relates to nationally coordinated public events to pressure the banks who were funding the Dakota Access Pipeline (DAPL) to stop doing so.

In Indianapolis, we had been working on defunding the Dakota Access Pipeline (DAPL) for several months. On November 15, 2016, a crowd of about 200 of us alongside Native Americans in traditional dress marched through downtown Indianapolis with our signs about defunding the pipeline. We stopped in front of two of the banks involved with funding the pipeline, Chase and PNC Bank. The crowd stood in silence as people went in to close their accounts. That day the group withdrew $110,000 dollars.

![](https://i0.wp.com/newconscientiousobjector.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/02/DEP_0135.jpg)

![](https://i0.wp.com/newconscientiousobjector.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/02/image-14.png)

![](https://i0.wp.com/newconscientiousobjector.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/02/DSC_0591.jpg)

![](https://i0.wp.com/newconscientiousobjector.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/02/DEP_0148.jpg)

#### Closing my Chase bank account

Yet my own effort to close my Chase bank account was much more difficult than I thought it would be.

Because of administrative changes, I first had a lot of trouble getting the forms to change my paycheck to direct deposit. It took time to set up paying bills. Also, I realized that I had initially chosen Chase bank because they had the most ATM locations. This was important because I don’t own a car. There can be inconveniences from defunding. I did it anyway.

![](https://i0.wp.com/newconscientiousobjector.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/02/chase-cicle.jpg)

I let my friends who were involved in defunding DAPL know that I was now ready to close my Chase account. I invited them to join me at the bank when I closed my account.

I went down to the Circle in the center of downtown Indianapolis where the Chase Tower dominates the Indianapolis skyline. I spent about an hour walking around the Circle with my sign, looking to see if anyone else had shown up from my local group. It is a little nerve wracking to be walking around by yourself like that, but, for better or worse, no one looks directly at you or engages you, for the most part.

I was also hoping to get a photo of the sign in front of Chase bank (this was requested as part of the national campaign). When I walked past Bridget, who sits on the Circle every day, crocheting, she asked me what the sign said, and we had a conversation about the importance of protecting our environment. She graciously took several photos for me, including the one above.

I had finally worked up the courage to enter the Chase Bank Tower to close my account.  I had no idea what the reaction to entering the bank with my sign would be. I just held it at my side, and then placed it next to my chair as I waited.  The bank officer greeted me with a smile and said someone would be with me shortly. He came back after about ten minutes to say he appreciated my patience—it was a busy time.

Mostly people coming into the bank ignored me, but there were a number of glances in my direction.

When I was shown into the banker’s office, she saw my sign, smiled, put her hands together and bowed to me, and said, “We are on the same page with this.” She put her finger to her lips with a smile indicating she shouldn’t be saying that, officially. She was very pleasant and helpful. When I left, she took my hand in both of hers.

As I was walking past the lobby officer when I left, I reached out my hand, which he took in both of his hands, giving me a big smile and a little bow as well. I told him I appreciated his patience with my freedom of speech, and he smiled and said, “Of course.”

My little bit was added to the total amount of personal money divested so far: $72,944,005.39 dollars according to defunddapl.org.

I felt a transfer of goodwill between me and those in the bank to such an extent that I returned later in the week to drop off three copies of the blog article I had written describing how well they had treated me and the whole defunding process. When the banker I had dealt with previously glanced up, she gave me a big smile and waved me in. She got up and again took my hand in hers and asked what she could do for me. She told me she and her husband had talked about our visit and the pipeline.

This is how our stories spread.

During meeting for business in February at North Meadow Circle of Friends, the meeting approved closing its Chase Bank account in solidarity with the #noDAPL movement.

# Refuse to normalize what is grotesque

*New Conscientious Objector (NewCO), 2026-02-18* · [Original post](https://newconscientiousobjector.com/2026/02/18/refuse-to-normalize-what-is-grotesque/)[^original-post]

These times of deep moral injury and chaos can become overwhelming. So many people have withdrawn into themselves.

I recently became aware of the website, **[Tending The In-Between.](https://tendingtheinbetween.substack.com/)** In these confusing times, it is a gift to discover a place that helps make sense of the conditions we find ourselves in. **“The way forward is not louder reaction. It is grounded awareness.”**

This grounded awareness is what we Quakers strive to attain. Yet, so many Friends are struggling to maintain this spiritual awareness. At a time when our friends and neighbors need this perspective, are we failing in our witness?

I have been led to believe that it is impossible to attain any justice as long as we continue to accept and benefit from the status quo. The term **incommensurable** applies. The current systems of politics and the economy are completely incompatible with alternative systems of justice.

Why aren’t more people, including Quakers, speaking out against these systems of injustice? The reasons for most people are related to the concept of the **‘economic draft.’**

![](https://i0.wp.com/newconscientiousobjector.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/02/unnamed-78.png)

The Economic Draft is the modern mechanism of conscription that weaponizes survival needs to force individuals into complicity with systems of extraction and violence. Individuals are “conscripted” not by law, but by manufactured scarcity—the threat of starvation, homelessness, and the loss of healthcare.

The concept of the NewCO (new conscientious objector) demonstrates how to escape from the economic draft. The new conscientious objector responds with the concepts of Mutual Aid, LANDBACK, and replacing police and prisons with community care and safety. That is what this website is devoted to.

> And the quiet refusal to normalize what is grotesque — without losing composure — is the most stabilizing force available right now.
> That is sovereignty.
> [Tending The In-Between](https://tendingtheinbetween.substack.com/p/the-collapse-of-response)

When the scope of wrongdoing feels vast, systemic, and untouchable, outrage turns into helplessness. Helplessness turns into fatigue. Fatigue turns into normalization. If I can’t change it, I adapt to it.
This is how horror becomes background noise. It is also how conscience dulls — not from evil intent, but from overload.

Notice when you begin to treat the unthinkable as routine. Notice when you feel flat instead of moved. Notice when outrage gives way to resignation. Not to shame yourself. To recalibrate.
Conscience is not loud. It is steady. It does not scream. It orients.
The collapse of response does not mean humanity is gone. It means humanity is overwhelmed.
The way forward is not louder reaction. It is grounded awareness.
Hold your moral line. Regulate your nervous system. Refuse to let repetition desensitize you. Stay clear without becoming chaotic.
You do not need to adapt to horror in order to survive it.
And the quiet refusal to normalize what is grotesque — without losing composure — is the most stabilizing force available right now.
That is sovereignty.

**T[he Collapse of Response. Why horror no longer lands — and what it takes to stay human when it doesn’t.

# Objection to War

*New Conscientious Objector (NewCO), 2026-02-28* · [Original post](https://newconscientiousobjector.com/2026/02/28/objection-to-war/)[^original-post]

What does it mean to be a peacemaker in these times of domestic and international war and violence? On this day, when this country attacked Iran?

What comes to me this morning is to tell the story of how President Obama worked so hard to get approval for the Iran Nuclear Deal. To remind people of when there was an administration that worked for peace. I hope this story might provide future peacemakers some ideas about working for peace. Might give us a little hope this morning.

On July 30, 2015, President Obama appealed directly to those of us supporting the deal, which included ongoing international inspections of Iran’s work to enrich fuel for nuclear power. The **international monitoring had been working** until the previous Trump administration unilaterally left the deal.

---

On **November 19, 2020**, I wrote about the consequences of **[Leaving Iran Nuclear Deal and War.](https://jeffkisling.com/2020/11/19/leaving-iran-nuclear-deal-and-war/)**

> “While Durbin and Nancy Pelosi were tracking the votes in their respective chambers, the president took a larger part and also played rougher in this fight than had been his custom. He accused Republicans of “making common cause” with Iran’s hard-liners. He stated that the alternatives were the deal or war.  Even some of his allies thought he’d gone a bit overboard with these statements, potentially alienating some undecided Democrats, and he pulled back from them. Obama responded to the requests by Pelosi and Durbin to make calls to wavering Democrats, more calls than he’d made on any previous legislation. He held special briefings in the White House for members of Congress; **he participated in a conference call with the outside groups on his side**.
> ”[How They Failed to Block the Iran Deal](http://www.nybooks.com/articles/archives/2015/oct/22/how-they-failed-block-iran-deal/?pagination=false&printpage=true)“, New York Times, 10/22/2015

Our work in Indiana to support the Iran deal began with the only time I have been on a conference call with President Barack Obama. The Friends Committee on National Legislation (FCNL) helped make that call possible. That speaks to the influence of FCNL in Washington, DC.

**July 31, 2015**

Last night President Obama spoke for half an hour by phone to activists who support him. He described how the Iran deal is a good deal for the United States and all the countries that joined in the negotiations in good faith that they would all agree to the deal. This is the agreement that the international community hammered out and supports. If Congress defeats this bill, that will likely end any influence the United States could have in the Middle East. Opponents of the bill only offer that we need a “better deal”, but have nothing to offer as to what that could possibly be. Those who say we should continue with sanctions don’t understand that is not possible now. Sanctions only work when the international community supports and enforces them. That won’t happen if they see the U.S. cannot agree on a foreign policy, as would be evident if this bill is defeated. There is also the question of who the sanctions hurt, which is the people of Iran, not their leaders. This feeds the movement to join terrorist organizations. An improved standard of living for the Iranian people should help mitigate that. The President specifically asked us to speak out to support this deal. **“In the absence of your voices, you are going to see the same array of voices that got us into the Iraq war, leading to a situation in which we forgo a historic opportunity and we are back on the path of potential military conflict,”**he said.

**August 27, 2015**

As a direct result of that call with President Obama, I’ve spent the past week, with the help of Erin Polley, AFSC, organizing the delivery of a petition with over 10,000 Indiana signatures supporting the Iran nuclear deal.  Members of North Meadow Circle of Friends, Indiana Moral Mondays, and MoveOn met with staff of Senator Joe Donnelly’s Indianapolis office yesterday.  Senator Donnelly had just stated his position, and said he now supports the deal. So this was a ‘thank you’ event, which the Senator’s staff indicated didn’t happen very often.

# Spirituality

*New Conscientious Objector (NewCO), 2026-03-11* · [Original post](https://newconscientiousobjector.com/2026/03/11/spirituality/)[^original-post]

The fundamental question that has been lurking in my mind is how do these new ideas of living together work in practice? Specifically, how are decisions made, and by whom? Mutual aid is based upon the rejection of hierarchical models. LANKBACK is about centering Indigenous leadership. Abolition is about changing from police and prisons to community care and safety.

Quakers believe the Spirit continues to guide us today. Our faith is dynamic, not static. Our form of worship is to gather together in silence for about an hour on Sunday morning, listening for what is sometimes called “that still, small voice” of the Spirit to guide us. Also fundamental to our spiritual practice is to try to be continually aware of the Spirit in every living moment.

As my research into the concepts of the economic draft, active objection, the NewCO (new conscientious objector) and resilience hubs have evolved, I’ve struggled to find ways to bring spirituality into those concepts, because I believe **spirituality must be the foundation** that they are based upon.

![](https://i0.wp.com/newconscientiousobjector.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/03/image-19.png)

---

As shown in the following mind map, a **Spiritual Foundation** is part of the NewCO (New Conscientious Objector). This branches to **Inner Light** or **Intersection with Indigenous Practices**.

![](https://i0.wp.com/newconscientiousobjector.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/03/image-18.png)

I believe our Quaker spiritual practices are uniquely positioned as a format for spiritual seeking and guidance for everyone, or at least for those who are not Indigenous. Even for those who profess to **not have a faith tradition** (referred to as **tacit knowledge**).

What little I know about Indigenous spiritual practices seems to indicate enough similarities that I could see spiritual gatherings of Indigenous, and non-native people who do or do not have a faith tradition, gathering together in a circle, in silence. [**NOTE**: I’ve been delving more into this research and will share what others have written and done related to these combined spiritual practices].

# Reflections

*New Conscientious Objector (NewCO), 2026-03-12* · [Original post](https://newconscientiousobjector.com/2026/03/12/reflections/)[^original-post]

> ***Every bombed village is my hometown. And every dead child is my child. Every grieving mother is my mother. Every crying father is my father. Every home turned to rubble is the home I grew up in. Every brother carrying the remains of his brother across borders is my brother. Every sister waiting for a sister who will never come home is my sister. Every one of these people is ours, just like we are theirs. We belong to them, and they belong to us.”***
> ***— James Baldwin***

It is paradoxical that during this time when I’ve been working on concepts for a just future, this country has been increasingly expanding its toxic politics and military might both around the world, and within our domestic society. There is a pervasive sense that it is all falling apart. Or it is the coming/ongoing collapse that is driving my work today.

Over the past several years I’ve been praying and doing research to try to understand how things have gone so wrong.

I’ve learned from Indigenous friends and experiences, the depth of the trauma that occurred, and continues to occur, as a result of the settler-colonization of their lands.

I’ve tried to understand how my faith community, Quakers, lost their/our way. I never will understand how it is possible to believe there is that of God in everyone and everything, and then be deeply involved in the dehumanization, the cultural and literal genocide, the damage and deaths of Native children and communities. Black and brown children and their communities.

The masks have come off to expose the extreme ugliness and depth of devastation of the capitalist system and its increasingly violent enforcement. Fundamental freedoms no longer exist. Freedoms which were essentially only applied for the dominate class in any case.

One of the most difficult things for Friends to accept is that we can no longer even have the illusion that our lobbying efforts are effective, as they once were. This is important because we only have so much energy, and I believe it should not be spent trying to tweak a fundamentally unjust system.

Some time ago I was searching for how to respond to these systems of injustice we are all embedded in. I was reminded of how I responded to another system of injustice I was confronted with, the Selective Service System (the draft). For the sake of my parents I tried to fit myself into the constraints of conscientious objector status.

But I couldn’t do it. I would have still been complicit in the systems of war. So I turned in my draft cards.

I thought back to that time, and realized I was, we all were, embedded in systems of injustice. I was led to the concepts of the current **economic draft.** The economic draft conscripts us to work in jobs that don’t reflect our values by the threats of the loss of healthcare associated with the job, of the requirement of a large income to pay off student debt. Or the poverty draft of targeting young men who don’t have good job prospects.

Were there ways we could **conscientious object** to the economic draft?

![](https://i0.wp.com/newconscientiousobjector.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/03/Spiritual-grounding-clay.png)

During these time of seeking, I’m grateful that a Quaker friend challenged us (Quakers) to remain faithful to the command to **“resist not evil.”** That concept was brought up to me by another Quaker back in the days of my struggles during the Vietnam War. I realized then, but had forgotten, how important that admonition was. Resistance legitimizes the unjust systems and absorbs you attention and energy. **You cannot make progress toward justice while you remain embedded in the systems of injustice.**

That history of **conscientious objection** and non-cooperation with the draft led me to the concept of **active objection**. Active objection turns our focus and energy towards systems of justice. To focus on Mutual Aid, LANDBACK, and replacing carceral systems with systems of community care, instead. To the concept of the **NewCO (New Conscientious Objector).** Which I will continue to write about on this blog.

# Authentic cross-cultural connections

*New Conscientious Objector (NewCO), 2026-03-16* · [Original post](https://newconscientiousobjector.com/2026/03/16/authentic-cross-cultural-connections/)[^original-post]

I am glad to see increased interest in the work of Indigenous peoples. But non-native people usually don’t know how to make connections with Native Americans.

One of the best ways to do that is by showing up at Indigenous-led events, such as the **Spring Equinox Celebration: Hub Blessing and Land Liberation** at the Great Plains Action Society’ s Urban Resilience HUB in Iowa City on March 21.

#### **Great Plain Action Society’s Urban Resilience HUB**

#### **Common pitfalls**

This increased interest reminds me of the common dangers to avoid when trying to connect with people of a different culture.. I created the following list, which has evolved from many cross-cultural experiences I’ve had through the years. And various educational opportunities I participated in.

* I received training to plan and implement nonviolent demonstrations related to the **Keystone XL pipeline** from the Rainforest Action Network.
* I led the Quaker meeting I attended in Indianapolis, North Meadow Circle of Friends, to implement the American Friends Service Committee’s **Quaker Social Change Ministry** program. That was designed to help Quakers move out of our meetinghouses and into the communities around us. The focus was on how to create such connections.
* At Sikowis’ suggestion, I attended the **National Network Assembly**, a conference aimed at people involved in justice work.
* I was fortunate to be asked to attend the **Buffalo Rebellion** training conference sponsored by the Great Plains Action Society and others.. The purpose was to bring together people who have been activists in their communities to receive more community organizing training.

![](https://i0.wp.com/newconscientiousobjector.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/03/image-32.png)

### **Don’t be a burden**

**The most important part of engaging with others is to avoid being a burden**. Oppressed peoples are stressed and don’t have the energy or inclination to try to educate others. Explanations aren’t very helpful in the first place, because my experience is that you only really learn by being present when you are invited.

### **Do NOT ask or expect to be taught**

There is a difference between expecting to be taught and accepting what someone is offering to teach you. Ronnie James, of Des Moines Mutual Aid, was very generous with his time and encouragement with me. He is a very effective organizer. He recognized our Wet’suwet’en vigil would be a chance to find allies for the work he does. Since then, I’ve seen how often, and how well he writes to educate others. And he always shows up. In the nearly three years I’ve known him, he and I have rarely missed being at our weekly food giveaway. And those times when he isn’t there, it is often because of other things related to his activism. He is involved in many things besides our food project.

### **Listen deeply-this is how you learn**

Think about what is being said. Learn the language, so to speak. Pay attention to body language and facial expressions. This is hard when people are wearing face masks, which are always required at our food project. No face mask, no participation. This is done to reduce the chance of any of us passing the virus on to others.

Observe common tasks and help do them. For example, every Saturday morning tables need to be set up outside, where the food boxes will be put for distribution. So you should do that if there is idle time. You don’t need to ask for permission. **It is expected that you will use your own initiative.** Because of everyone being aware of what needs to be done, and doing it, our work is done really efficiently. As Ronnie says, at the end of the hour you will be tired, sweaty and felling good. Truth.

> **It can take a long time (months or years) to understand all that is involved in the work you are participating in**.

### **Do NOT offer suggestions/leadership until invited to do so**

It can take a long time (months or years) to understand all that is involved in the work you are participating in. It has taken a lot of work, trial and error, for those involved in the community you are connecting with to get things to function as they are..

The rest of the list is self-explanatory. Accepting being vulnerable is likely the most difficult part of this. You are being vulnerable just by doing what it takes to join in the work, to show up. When uncomfortable things happen, they are often not your fault. Try not to take things personally.
